cases.explain: Предположение is the predicate noun after было (was), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: «Нет и нет», — ответила она себе теперь без малейшего ___.
cases.translation: "No, and no," she answered herself now without the slightest hesitation.
cases.explain: The preposition без (without) governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Она подъехала к низкому ___ю Нижегородской станции.
cases.translation: She drove up to the low building of the Nizhny Novgorod station.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Сказала она ему, подавая ___ с деньгами.
cases.translation: She said to him, handing over the purse with money.
cases.explain: Кошелек is the direct object of подавая (handing over); this inanimate masculine noun has the same form as the nominative.

cases.sentence: Мы с ___ом Вронским также не нашли этого удовольствия.
cases.translation: Count Vronsky and I likewise did not find that pleasure.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Сидя на звездообразном ___е в ожидании поезда.
cases.translation: Sitting on the star-shaped sofa, waiting for the train.
cases.explain: The preposition на (on) indicating location governs the prepositional case.

reading.ru: «Опять я понимаю все!» — сказала себе Анна, как только коляска тронулась и, покачиваясь, загремела по мелкой мостовой, и опять одно за другим стали сменяться впечатления.
reading.question: What happens to Anna's thoughts as the carriage sets off?
options: She feels she understands everything again as impressions begin to change one after another
She decides to return home at once
reading.correct: She feels she understands everything again as impressions begin to change one after another
reading.explain: As the carriage starts moving, Anna says to herself that she understands everything again, and impressions begin succeeding one another.

reading.ru: Борьба за существование и ненависть — одно, что связывает людей».
reading.question: What idea from Yashvin does Anna recall?
options: That struggle for existence and hatred are what bind people together
reading.correct: That struggle for existence and hatred are what bind people together
reading.explain: Anna recalls Yashvin's remark that struggle for existence and hatred are the only things binding people.

reading.ru: «Мы с графом Вронским также не нашли этого удовольствия, хотя и много ожидали от него».
reading.question: What does Anna think she and Vronsky failed to find, despite expecting much from it?
reading.explain: Anna reflects that she and Count Vronsky did not find that pleasure either, though they had expected much from it.

reading.ru: «Чего он искал во мне? Любви не столько, сколько удовлетворения тщеславия».
reading.question: What does Anna conclude Vronsky sought in her?
options: Satisfaction of vanity rather than love
reading.correct: Satisfaction of vanity rather than love
reading.explain: Anna concludes he sought not so much love as the satisfaction of vanity.

reading.ru: Он взял от меня все, что мог, и теперь я не нужна ему.
reading.question: What does Anna believe about Vronsky's feelings now?
options: He took all he could from her and no longer needs her
He loves her more than ever
He wants to marry her immediately
reading.correct: He took all he could from her and no longer needs her
reading.explain: Anna thinks he has taken everything he could from her and now has no need of her.

reading.ru: Моя любовь все делается страстнее и себелюбивее, а его все гаснет и гаснет, и вот от чего мы расходимся»,
reading.question: How does Anna describe the difference between her love and Vronsky's?
options: Hers grows more passionate and selfish while his keeps fading
Hers is fading while his grows
reading.correct: Hers grows more passionate and selfish while his keeps fading
reading.explain: Anna says her love becomes ever more passionate and self-centered while his keeps dying out, which is why they are drifting apart.

reading.ru: А где кончается любовь, там начинается ненависть.
reading.question: What does Anna conclude about love and hatred?
reading.explain: Anna states directly that where love ends, hatred begins.

reading.ru: Вспомнив об Алексее Александровиче, она тотчас с необыкновенную живостью представила себе его как живого пред собой, с его кроткими безжизненными потухшими глазами, синими жилами на белых руках, интонациями и треском пальцев.
reading.question: How does Anna picture Alexei Alexandrovich when she recalls him?
options: With meek, lifeless, dulled eyes, blue veins on white hands, and cracking finger joints
reading.correct: With meek, lifeless, dulled eyes, blue veins on white hands, and cracking finger joints
reading.explain: The passage describes his meek, lifeless, dulled eyes, blue veins on white hands, his intonations, and the cracking of his fingers.

reading.ru: «Ну, я получу развод и буду женой Вронского».
reading.question: What future does Anna imagine for herself regarding Vronsky?
options: Getting a divorce and becoming Vronsky's wife
reading.correct: Getting a divorce and becoming Vronsky's wife
reading.explain: Anna imagines obtaining a divorce and becoming Vronsky's wife.

reading.ru: «А Сережа перестанет спрашивать или думать о моих двух мужьях?»
reading.question: What worry does Anna have about her son Seryozha?
options: Whether he will stop asking or thinking about her two husbands
reading.correct: Whether he will stop asking or thinking about her two husbands
reading.explain: Anna wonders whether Seryozha will stop asking or thinking about her having two husbands.

reading.ru: Разве все мы не брошены на свет за тем, только чтобы ненавидеть друг друга и потому мучить себя и других?
reading.question: What bleak thought does Anna have about humanity?
options: That everyone is born only to hate and torment one another
That everyone is born to seek happiness
That love is the purpose of life
reading.correct: That everyone is born only to hate and torment one another
reading.explain: Anna wonders whether everyone is put into the world only to hate one another and thereby torment themselves and others.

reading.question: What question does Pyotr ask Anna as they approach the station?
options: Whether she wants to go as far as Obiralovka
Whether she wants to return home
Whether she wants to see Vronsky's mother
reading.correct: Whether she wants to go as far as Obiralovka
reading.explain: Pyotr asks whether he should take her ticket as far as Obiralovka.

reading.ru: Она совсем забыла, куда и зачем она ехала, и только с большим усилием могла понять вопрос.
reading.question: What does Anna's reaction to Pyotr's question reveal about her state of mind?
options: She had completely forgotten where and why she was going
She was fully alert and focused
reading.correct: She had completely forgotten where and why she was going
reading.explain: The text says she had entirely forgotten where and why she was travelling and only understood the question with great effort.

reading.ru: Сидя на звездообразном диване в ожидании поезда, она с отвращением глядя на входивших и выходивших, все они были противны ей.
reading.question: How does Anna feel while waiting for the train on the star-shaped sofa?
options: She looks with disgust at people coming and going, finding them all repulsive
She strikes up a friendly conversation
reading.correct: She looks with disgust at people coming and going, finding them all repulsive
reading.explain: The text says she looked with disgust at those entering and leaving, all of whom were repulsive to her.
